utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you mention the names of these persons?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS FWS-198 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no. One, I could mention one, but one doesn't really mean much to you. It was a long time ago.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you tell me whether you know, whether you ever made any statements in this sense, who was in charge of exchanges in the KP Dom?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS FWS-198 [Resumed]
utterances.text: According to some information, we were told that it was Boro Ivanovic. Perhaps that was correct; perhaps that was not correct. Vojislav Maksimovic, Petko Cancar.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. We already talked about a statement that you gave to the investigators of the OTP. Do you remember having said to the investigators of the Office of the Prosecutor that you were in Room 20 after having stayed in Room 18?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS FWS-198 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it's possible that I made this permutation. I went to 16 and to 20, and then from 20 to 18.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you recall when you were in Room 20, in which period?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS FWS-198 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was the month of -- no, it was after seven months.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The month of October?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS FWS-198 [Resumed]
utterances.text: The month of October, that's when I was in Room 20.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That is to say that, from October onwards, you were in Room 20.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS FWS-198 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but I was not in Room 20 for a long time. A month or two. I don't know. Nobody kept such records as to how long you would be in one room and how long you would be in another room.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember having said to the investigators of the OTP that when you were in Room 20, Husko Rikalo was taken out?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS FWS-198 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. In Room 20? No, no. He was taken out when I was in number 16. Possibly I made a mistake.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In order to be as clear as possible, because of what we might do after this, is it correct that you said that you were in Room 20 when Husko Rikalo was taken out?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS FWS-198 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I was not in Room 20. I was in Room 16, not Room 20.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it necessary for me to read your statement? And if it is not necessary, what would your comment be? Why did you say that you were in Room 20 then?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS FWS-198 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, you can read it out. No problem with that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: I object, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: "I remember --"

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Smith.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: The witness has said he possibly made a mistake.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Well, I realise that, and what weight can be given to this almost completely escapes me. But the Defence is entitled to show he's made an inconsistent statement and to have it shown firmly. So you proceed, Mr. Bakrac.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could counsel please quote the page that he is quoting from.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Did you get that message from the interpreter, Mr. Bakrac?

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I did. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: "I remember that once when I was in Room 20 Husko Rikalo was taken out."

utterances.speaker: WITNESS FWS-198 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes, possibly I could have made a mistake, but what can I say now? I signed that statement, the one I gave, and if I signed it, I have to stand by it. That is only natural.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it correct that this is the first time today that you stated this, and that you did not say this in the Centre for Security in Sarajevo or to the investigators of the OTP that you heard a certain Zelja say what you said before the break - I don't want to repeat it again - and that you saw Muniz Veib --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS FWS-198 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Munib Veiz.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Munib Veiz, that he got out of the office --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS FWS-198 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Nurko Nisic?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, Nurko Nisic.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS FWS-198 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, exactly. I saw it with my own eyes. Zoran Vladicic could be mine witness. Zoran Vladicic could be my witness. I'll be his witness; he'll be mine. We stood at the door together when he walked out of the room, covered with blood. I did not say it, but --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm going to read to you now exactly what you said at the Security Centre in Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: The interpreters do want you to give them the page number, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is identification number ID 311. In B/C/S, it is page 4, paragraph 2, somewhere around the middle of the page.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: "Nurko Nisic from Foca, Deputy Commander of the Public Security Station in Foca, was taken out in such a way and every time returned bloody from the beatings."

utterances.speaker: WITNESS FWS-198 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Exactly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: "I saw this through the window of my room, and I heard from the prisoners that he was beaten by a certain Zelja, aged about 35, dark-haired, earlier employed in the Elektrodistribucija," the power supply.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS FWS-198 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Exactly, that's exactly the way it was. "Nurko Nisic, the first time when I saw him all bloody. I saw him with my own eyes. I can confirm that through Zoran Vladicic if he wants to admit to that as well. He was not taken out only once, he was taken every five or ten days until he left the compound, and after that he never returned."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, I shall repeat a part of this sentence again. "I heard from the prisoners that he was beaten by a certain Zelja."

utterances.speaker: WITNESS FWS-198 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I heard it when I was being questioned by Zoran Vladicic, I heard his words. "Now you're going to see how Zelja administers beatings." At that moment, I did not know who he was beating. When I finished my interview with Zoran Vladicic, I signed the statement and I went into the hallway through the door and then Nurko Nisic got out from the left arcade, there was blood flowing down his face, and only then I realised that it was Zelja beating Nurko Nisic.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said that you realised only then. When did you realise that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS FWS-198 [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I got out into the hall. Nobody had to tell me after that. As soon as he was going there every five or ten days, he was being taken out to the administrative building every five or ten days when he came in all bloody and black and blue. Gentlemen, let me apologise for having to say this: Nurko Nisic could not even walk because he was beaten on the testicles, on the head. And then when he would get a bit better, then he would be taken out and beaten.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Just a moment. I understand that you are very involved in all of this, but if you could speak just a little more slowly. The translators are having trouble keeping up with you. Yes, Mr. Bakrac.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Still, I do not know what is correct out of the two. Did you hear from the prisoner that he was beaten by Zelja or what you said today; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS FWS-198 [Resumed]
utterances.text: What I said today is correct and I confirm that and I stand by it, and if I have to I'm going to sign a document once again. Let the Court give me any kind of document and I'm going to sign it and I'm going to confirm that Zelja beat him, and that I saw him after that with my very own eyes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you know if Zelja was a military policeman at the time, or a military, or what was he at the time when that went on? Is it true that before the break you said that you were interviewed by Inspector Vladicic when you went for interview the third time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS FWS-198 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [No translation].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: Sorry, Your Honour, I believe the answer wasn't translated to the question that was given.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: What do you say the answer was?

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: I, as you know --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Did you hear an answer, Mr. Bakrac?

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I heard that he said, "I don't know."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you say that, on the third occasion, you were interviewed by Inspector Vladicic and you are confirming that. Do you remember that, on page four of your statement to the Prosecutor, you said that on the third occasion, you were interviewed by somebody you did not know?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS FWS-198 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I said there was this tall, dark, around 35, slim, and that other inspector, Koprivica, they were together.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. In addition to the pistol that you said was found at your place, did you have any other weapon?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS FWS-198 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. No. Nothing. I did not have anything else.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you participate in the fighting between the 18th [as interpreted] and the 16th of April?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS FWS-198 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I did not. I didn't want to. Had I wanted to, I would have either been dead by now or wouldn't be here today.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Excuse me, Your Honour. In the transcript, perhaps it was my mistake, it says 18th to the 16th, but what I meant was the 8th to the 16th.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: In case there was some error, do you think you should ask it again so that the dates are clear? I thought at the time that you must have been saying the 8th and it was just misinterpreted, but it might be safer, if you want to take the point clearly, to ask it of him again.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it true that between the 8th until the 17th of April, you took part in the fighting?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS FWS-198 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, and had I participated there, I wouldn't be here because I would be either dead or living somewhere in Bosnia.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I shall now read to you a part of the statement and can you confirm that you gave it to the Sarajevo Security Service. "Between the 8th and the 17th April, I joined a smaller unit which was offering resistance to the aggressor from the localities of Sahovac and Sistet." Yes or no about that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: There are two things. First, you didn't give the page number, and the second you read it at the rate of knots. It's very easy when you are reading something to speed up, but it's very hard on the interpreters.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise, Your Honour. It is page 2, ID-311, third paragraph, again, somewhere in the middle of the page and that is how the sentence begins.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: "In the period between the 8th and the 17th of April, I joined a smaller unit which offered resistance to the aggressor from the localities of Sahovac and Sistet."

utterances.speaker: WITNESS FWS-198 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sukovac.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sahovac, that is what it says here, and Sistet.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS FWS-198 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I joined with the women and the children and the elderly. I did not join the combatants or the army or carry a rifle because I was taken for interviews two or three times and I was on -- I wasn't on any list. To this day, I'm not on any list as a person who had a weapon. Because those who had weapons, Zoran Vladicic showed me the list with all the names of people who had some kind of weapons. Had I had such a weapon, had I carried such a weapon, I suppose I would have been on that list and then would not have been here, so that is my case. I did not really read it very thoroughly when I gave this statement in Sarajevo and there are some errors. There is yet another error in this text, perhaps you will find it, but I never carried a rifle and I stand by what I say. It is my mistake that I signed this without reading it beforehand, but ...

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Witness. I have no further questions. Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Re-examination, Mr. Smith.

utterances.speaker: MR. SMITH
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Thank you, sir -- I'm sorry. Thank you very much for giving evidence. You may leave but just wait until the blinds are pulled down so that you won't be seen from the public area.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Uertz-Retzlaff.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honour, before the next witness comes in, I have to inform the Court about the following: During the lunch break, I was informed that this witness wants, in addition to the already granted pseudonym and image alteration, he requests voice alteration. I spoke with him then, and he said that he was under the impression that he would have both, and if he did not request it, it was his mistake. His problem is that he was -- is it now -- are we in open session? I would then request to go into private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: We are now back in public session. Yes, Ms. Uertz-Retzlaff -- sorry. Would you take the solemn declaration, please, sir.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Sit down, please. Examined by Ms. Uertz-Retzlaff:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Witness.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS FWS-66
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, you have been granted the requests you had in relation to your security, so we have to avoid mentioning your name. In these proceedings, you have the number 66. If you now look at the piece of paper in front of you, the name under number 66, is that your name?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS FWS-66
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The date under your name, is that your birthday?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS FWS-66
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The name under your birthday, is that your brother's name?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS FWS-66
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So, Witness, when you wish to refer to your brother, do not mention his name, just say "my brother." And there are also three more names on this list. Whenever you want to mention these names, please do not say the names but say the number.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honour, the Prosecution would like to enter this document into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Mr. Bakrac, I won't ask you every time about this. If you do object to any of them, let me know. Is that all right if I proceed on that basis?

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honours. Yes, it is quite all right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Thank you. That will be Exhibit P401, and it shall be under seal.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, what is your ethnicity?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS FWS-66
utterances.text: Bosniak Muslim.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where were you born?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS FWS-66
utterances.text: Foca.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you married?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS FWS-66
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you have children; and if so, how many?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS FWS-66
utterances.text: Yes; two.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where did you live before the war; in which town and in which part of the town?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS FWS-66
utterances.text: In the centre of Foca.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How many inhabitants lived in Foca before the war?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS FWS-66
utterances.text: There were 40.000 in the municipality as such; 40.513 was the population of the municipality of Foca, according to the last census.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was the ethnic composition of these inhabitants?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS FWS-66
utterances.text: According to the last census, is that what you mean?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, and the ethnic composition.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS FWS-66
utterances.text: Yes. Well, it was 51 to 52 were Bosniaks; about 46 were Serbs; and others, the rest, that is, Croats and other minorities.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: To which region of Bosnia did Foca belong? Did it have a special name, this region?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS FWS-66
utterances.text: It was at the time called the Upper Drina region.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did this include; which municipalities?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS FWS-66
utterances.text: That region, it incorporated Foca, Gorazde, Rudo, Visegrad, Rogatici, and Cajnice.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was Foca the biggest town in this Gornji Podrinje?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS FWS-66
utterances.text: In terms of the population number, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was it a cultural centre of the region?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS FWS-66
utterances.text: Well, it was Gorazde largely.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Foca, before the war, was it a centre of Muslim culture in Bosnia and Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS FWS-66
utterances.text: Yes, yes, it was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What were the buildings belonging to this Muslim culture?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS FWS-66
utterances.text: Well, to begin with, it was the so-called Prijeka Carsija from the Turkish rule, Turkish era, but there were eleven other mosques in the town too.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was the oldest mosque?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS FWS-66
utterances.text: Aladza mosque.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How old was it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS FWS-66
utterances.text: Well, it was built around 1500, but I wouldn't know exactly; 1500-something.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was it a well-known mosque in Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS FWS-66
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Where exactly did you live in Foca? Can you specify maybe the blocks? Did they have a special name in the area where you lived?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS FWS-66
utterances.text: At first I lived in Donje Polje, and then in the centre.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you lived in the centre, did your region have a particular name?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS FWS-66
utterances.text: Centre, centre, that's what it was called. The centre neighbourhood community. My family house was in Donje Polje.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was your profession before the war?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS FWS-66
utterances.text: Well, at first I worked as a teacher in a school, and then I went to serve the army. After that, in the municipal department of the Territorial Defence, that's where I worked, and then in the municipal committee of the League of Communists.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, I will ask you now several specifics about your position in the institutions you just mentioned, but I would like you not to mention the exact position you had; rather, refer to, let's say, "management" or "high-ranking" or something like that, but not your particular position.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS FWS-66
utterances.text: I was in the staff of the Territorial Defence. And you don't want me to mention the place, do you?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I would like to know from you: While you were in the TO, did you have a rank?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS FWS-66
utterances.text: Yes; captain.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When did you have a function in the TO; in which years?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS FWS-66
utterances.text: From 1976 until 1980.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In your --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS FWS-66
utterances.text: Professionally, I mean. I was paid for that work.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. Did you have a rather high rank in the TO staff?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS FWS-66
utterances.text: Well, you want me to say what I was?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No. Don't say what it was, just answer yes or no. I just asked you if you had a rather high rank within the TO staff.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS FWS-66
utterances.text: Rather high.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In your capacity in the TO, did you ever meet the accused, Mr. Krnojelac?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS FWS-66
utterances.text: Yes, and I knew him before too.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did he have a rank?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS FWS-66
utterances.text: Yes; captain first class.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was this a higher rank than you had?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS FWS-66
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What exactly did he do in the TO? What was his position?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS FWS-66
utterances.text: He was the commander of the TO detachment under the combat order.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you meet him during your time in the TO, during, for instance, trainings?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS FWS-66
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you met, did you talk together? Did you spend time together?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS FWS-66
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said that you were in the TO till 1980. Did he continue to be active in the TO?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS FWS-66
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When did you meet him last at such trainings?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS FWS-66
utterances.text: Well, as I was also, for quite a long time, on the wartime assignment, even when I changed my job, I attended the military drills, until around 1976.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Can you just wait a moment?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS FWS-66
utterances.text: 1986, excuse me. 1986.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: We seem to be getting both the witness' voice in the original language and the translation at the same time. I don't know whether this is because of the voice distortion, but if there is something to be turned off, I myself would be very grateful.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Sorry, Your Honour, I do not have this problem.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: You're lucky. But the witness' own voice is drowning out most of the translation for me.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: But I would not know how to solve this problem.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: I think I've just been told how to. I've just used the volume control for the remote witness. He isn't very remote, but apparently that's the one that it comes in on. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, you said you had the last training together in 1986. Do you know if Mr. Krnojelac continued to be involved in the TO until the war started?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS FWS-66
utterances.text: Afterwards, I don't know. I believe so.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What makes you believe that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS FWS-66
utterances.text: Well, I did not hear about his being replaced.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Before the war, where did you work? And please have in mind not to mention exactly your position.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS FWS-66
utterances.text: In the municipal committee of the League of Communists, the then municipal committee.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And before the war, did you join any of the new parties?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS FWS-66
utterances.text: No, I continued as a member of that party.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So does that mean when the multi-party system started, your party still functioned and remained as a party and you stayed in there, is that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS FWS-66
utterances.text: Yes, until the elections, I kept that particular job, I held that job. And after the elections, I continued in that party.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The party you were in before, before the multi-party system started, was it a big party? Was it a party with a mixed ethnic background?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS FWS-66
utterances.text: Yes, indeed. It was the only party in the former Yugoslavia, the main party. And we were all in it, the majority.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You are smiling at Mr. Krnojelac. This was actually also my next question. Was Mr. Krnojelac also in this party and were you actually together on the board?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS FWS-66
utterances.text: Yes. He was a member, but we were not together. He was with the party organisation in the school in which he worked, and in the school, there was a party organisation.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In addition to the -- knowing him from the TO and knowing him from the communist party, did you know him privately and did you socialise with him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS FWS-66
utterances.text: Well, we were not friends, but we used to meet.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You are looking at the accused, Mr. Krnojelac. When you speak about Mr. Krnojelac, you are referring to the accused in this courtroom, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS FWS-66
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, an objection perhaps of a principle nature. "You look at Mr. Krnojelac," and then "is the accused here," so the Prosecutor has already answered. The question is the answer. "You are looking at Mr. Krnojelac."

utterances.speaker: WITNESS FWS-66
utterances.text: I knew him personally.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: I think that is so, but it is very clear that he has been looking at the accused and calling him Mr. Krnojelac throughout the whole of his evidence. So we have no problem that it is the accused to whom he is referring. I don't think you need to ask any further questions about that.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. And I was also only referring to them both looking at each other.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know if he was married and if he had children?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS FWS-66
utterances.text: Yes. He was married. He had four children.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Four what children; four sons or daughters, or both?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS FWS-66
utterances.text: Four sons.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know the names of the sons?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS FWS-66
utterances.text: I know the name of one of them; Bozidar. I don't know the others' names. I can't remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And this Bozidar, was he the oldest, the youngest, or in between?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS FWS-66
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How were the interethnic relations before the war? I'm referring to Foca only.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS FWS-66
utterances.text: You mean just before the war broke out or before the war?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Before the war, let's say 1990, something like this.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS FWS-66
utterances.text: Well, interethnic relations were fine until the multi-party elections occurred. We were all together. We worked together. We socialised.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when the multi-party system started, how did this change and why?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS FWS-66
utterances.text: Then, people started splitting up these two sides, at least in Foca. Socialising stopped. Restaurants were divided. Affairs started in Foca like the Focatrans affair. Until the war broke out -- by the time the war broke out, everything was divided.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell me the main political parties that influenced people before the war?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS FWS-66
utterances.text: The SDA and the SDS, the leading parties.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The SDA, what did it stand for? Did you ever attend a rally and can you tell us?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS FWS-66
utterances.text: I did not attend rallies because I did not belong there. I remained in the SDP party, and this other one was practically mono-ethnic, representing Bosniaks only.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when you say "Bosniaks", you mean Muslims, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS FWS-66
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Although you did not attend the rally of the SDA, did you nevertheless hear what their motto was or what they were focussing on?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS FWS-66
utterances.text: At a big rally that was held at the conference of the Cehotina and the Drina rivers, their motto was that the Drina will no longer flow bloody, and that is the motto under which this rally was held. They were actually referring to the slaughters that took place in 1941 and in 1942 in Foca.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was the motto of the SDS?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS FWS-66
utterances.text: As far as I read it then, wherever there was a Serb house, that was Serb land, and also wherever there was a Serb grave. And that that's the way it would be.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did the SDS politicians, what did they say about Muslims and Croats?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS FWS-66
utterances.text: First of all, this big rally, there were some representatives of the Croat people and from the leadership of the SDS. The SDA already then linked its flags with the HDZ, meaning that they would be more inclined towards Croatia than towards Serbia although there were not many Croats there, because we were almost at the border with Serbia and we had more contact with Serbia than with Croatia.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How did the SDS party and their politicians react to this?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS FWS-66
utterances.text: Are you talking about this rally and all of that?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm talking generally about the rally and about the politicians, the SDS politicians. How did they react to this?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS FWS-66
utterances.text: Well, probably on the basis of this SDA rally, in response to that, they organised a rally at the stadium in Foca and another one at the school centre in the amphitheatre.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During this rally, were there ever threats made against the other ethnic groups?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS FWS-66
utterances.text: Yes. I heard that they were made and graffiti appeared on different buildings and institutions, saying "This is Serbia," et cetera.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But were threats made against Muslims or Croats and, if so, what was threatened?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS FWS-66
utterances.text: As far as I heard then, these were threats that a people would be exterminated unless they joined Serbia.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who made those threats? Can you recall anyone in particular?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS FWS-66
utterances.text: I learnt about all of this from the press, from the newspapers, and from other people. I was not at these rallies, but this was said by the leading people of the SDS, Maksimovic, Ostojic, Karadzic, Plavsic, Kilibarda and the others.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: This division among these people and the threats, how did it make you feel?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS FWS-66
utterances.text: Awful. The Bosniak people lived in great fear because it was noticed that weapons were being distributed and placed on all heights around Foca, stating that this was because of military exercises.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You mentioned that Mr. Krnojelac was together with you in the communist party. Did he remain in the communist party? Did you observe him?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS FWS-66
utterances.text: No. He did not remain there, because I left lists in my office with the names of all of those who were in the SDP and he was not among them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know if he became a member of any other party?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS FWS-66
utterances.text: Probably the national party, the SDS, I mean.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say "probably," does it mean you know?

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: I would have thought that the answer to that was clearly he does not know, and that's why he used the word "probably." It is a leading question, Ms. Uertz-Retzlaff. You can ask him specifically: "Did you know that fact or did you merely hear it or are you guessing?"

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Is that the objection, Mr. Bakrac?

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, thank you, that is precisely what I wish to say.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, you said probably he was in a nationalist party. But why do you think so? What makes you believe that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS FWS-66
utterances.text: Well, I saw him several times going to the Ribarski restaurant where Maksimovic, Ostojic, and the others would come. (redacted) (redacted).

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who met at the Ribarski restaurant? Was it party meetings?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS FWS-66
utterances.text: Yes. Muslims, as of late, had not entered that restaurant.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You have mentioned several people like Maksimovic, Ostojic. Who were they?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS FWS-66
utterances.text: They were the ideologues of that party. They are both from that area, and they were among the main founders of that party in Foca.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How often did you see them at gatherings in the Ribarski restaurant before the war?

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Objection, Your Honour. The witness said that he did not see them at rallies but saw them go to the Ribarski restaurant where meetings were held, (redacted).

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: But the question was: "How often did you see them at gatherings in the Ribarski restaurant," which is precisely where he said that they were. My only query about it is: Which party were they the ideologues of? That, I think, would tie it in. I don't think there's anything wrong with the question, Mr. Bakrac.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, since I speak the same language as the witness, I know exactly what he said. He said that he saw the accused going to Ribarski restaurant.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] He did not say that he saw their meeting.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Your objection is recorded in this way: "The witness said that he did not see them at rallies but saw them go to the Ribarski restaurant where meetings were held," and that was precisely what the question was. What's wrong with that? He had earlier said that they met at the Ribarski restaurant, and he added that Muslims did not at that time enter that restaurant. He's placed them in the restaurant, not at rallies.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I understood the witness exactly as he had said it. He saw the accused going to Ribarski restaurant where Maksimovic and the others were. Let the question be whether he saw them going to the restaurant together.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: I think that that is of the most extreme technicality, if I may say so, Mr. Bakrac. The question was a fair one on the answers which have been given. If the answers which were given are different in the interpretation to what you heard, well, then, you have a perfectly fair objection to take. But on the answers that are recorded, it was a fair question.

utterances.speaker: MR. BAKRAC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I am convinced that it is a technical mistake, and that is the problem here, that we have interpretation. Even intonations and parts of sentences and the word order can change a meaning. I understand that problem. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: If you do see anything where you think it has been incorrectly translated, then please let us know. We don't want there to be any errors about it. But unless you can show us that there is something wrong with this translation we have, in my view, the question was a fair one. You proceed, Ms. Uertz-Retzlaff.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Witness, these politicians you just mentioned, to which party did they belong, those politicians you mentioned as ideologues?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS FWS-66
utterances.text: All of them belonged to the SDS party. Every man from Foca, every person from Foca, will know how to answer that: that meetings were held at the Ribarski restaurant. They waited for them to see when they would come to the Ribarski restaurant; Ostojic, Maksimovic, Kornjaca from Cajnice, and the others. That is where our local people waited for them and attended meetings. I never entered that restaurant during that time, nor anyone else but them, and that is what every person knows, that that was held there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How often did you see such meetings of the SDS party in the restaurant?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS FWS-66
utterances.text: Very often, (redacted).

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: From your window, could you see the restaurant?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS FWS-66
utterances.text: Yes, I could see the restaurant.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said that Mr. Krnojelac went there. Did you ever see him go to the restaurant together with these politicians?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS FWS-66
utterances.text: No, not with them but with the people from Foca.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ever learn that he had a function in the SDS?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS FWS-66
utterances.text: No, I did not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How often did you see Mr. Krnojelac attend meetings in the restaurant?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS FWS-66
utterances.text: A few times. Two or three times I saw him going there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you recall when you saw him going to the meetings? Do you recall the year or even the month?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS FWS-66
utterances.text: No, no, I cannot recall.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you saw him going there, what did he wear?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS FWS-66
utterances.text: Civilian clothes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When did the war in Foca break out?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS FWS-66
utterances.text: Officially, on the 8th of April, 1992.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say "officially," what do you mean? Is there also an unofficial beginning?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS FWS-66
utterances.text: A day earlier, Abid Ramovic, a policeman, was killed who was trying to rescue a woman who had been wounded near the former railway station. That brought great fear among the people. On the 7th of April, around 10.00 in the morning, the main attack on Foca took place.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was included in this attack with regard to weapons?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS FWS-66
utterances.text: Both shells and infantry weapons.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How long did the fighting last?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS FWS-66
utterances.text: For a few days.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did you do during these days?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS FWS-66
utterances.text: I hid in shelters and I was in my apartment.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ever get involved in the fighting?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS FWS-66
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was the fighting all over Foca or was it concentrated in certain neighbourhoods?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS FWS-66
utterances.text: There was shooting from all sides, but most of it was directed at Donje Polje, the neighbourhood of Donje Polje.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is this a Muslim neighbourhood?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS FWS-66
utterances.text: Majority. Majority Muslim.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were houses destroyed during this initial fighting?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS FWS-66
utterances.text: Yes, they were.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know in which part of the town houses were destroyed during this initial fighting?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS FWS-66
utterances.text: During the first days, as far as I managed to find out, a few houses were destroyed near Krnojelac's house. Even his was ablaze.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you see that or did you hear about it?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS FWS-66
utterances.text: No, I could not see it because I did not dare move about. But I heard about it from others.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were these Serb houses destroyed deliberately or during the fighting?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS FWS-66
utterances.text: There wasn't any fighting there, only a little. I think this was done intentionally.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is there a reason why someone would destroy the house of the accused Krnojelac?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS FWS-66
utterances.text: As far as I heard -- actually, I knew that one of his sons had a cafe in that house and that on the eve of the war, these sort of extremists of the SDS had gathered there. But I did not see that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who told you? How do you know that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS FWS-66
utterances.text: That's what people said. That is what people said just before the war broke out; people talked about where, who gathered, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did you hear about the cafe of the son of the accused?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS FWS-66
utterances.text: Well, I heard that that was one of the places where the extreme wing of the SDS gathered. Some kind of extremists. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What do you call extremists? What does that mean when you say it? You said the extreme wing of the SDS. What does that mean?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS FWS-66
utterances.text: Well, people like Tuta Janjic, people like that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who was that, Tuta Janjic?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS FWS-66
utterances.text: A criminal.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What does such a person have to do with the SDS?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS FWS-66
utterances.text: He carried out certain actions.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You knew Mr. Krnojelac. Did you ever hear that he was an extremist?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS FWS-66
utterances.text: No, I never heard that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Given the fact that the house of the accused, Krnojelac, was destroyed during the war, do you know where he lived during the war?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS FWS-66
utterances.text: After his house was destroyed, you mean?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS FWS-66
utterances.text: I heard that he moved into an apartment, the apartment of a doctor, because painters, who were detained together with us, were taken out to paint that apartment.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when you say "doctor," do you mean a Muslim doctor?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS FWS-66
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: I think it's now 4.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Thank you. Before we adjourn, there are two things I want to say. Firstly, this courtroom is being used tomorrow for another case so that it would be unsafe, I think, to leave any materials around. The Defence bar table will have to accommodate six counsel and they take up a lot of room so particularly the Defence counsel better move all their stuff out. The other thing that I want to point out is that the criticism of the previous application for voice distortion which I implied in my praise on the way in which the last one was presented, was not directed at anyone in the Prosecution team here but was directed at the Victims' and Witnesses' Unit which appears, unfortunately, to believe that protective measures only have to be asked for to be granted, and it was to emphasise that a basis,some objective basis must be shown before protective measures are granted. We will adjourn now in this case until Monday at 9.30. --

utterances.speaker: MS. UERTZ-RETZLAFF
utterances.text: Your Honour, there is now a break. I think the next day is the 23rd.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: Yes, of course, we've changed the week, you're quite right. Thank you very much. Until 9.30 on the 23rd.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HUNT
utterances.text: at 4.02 p.m., to be reconvened on Thursday the 23rd day of November, 2000, at 9.30 a.m. 25
